quest.title: Realm of Fog and Wind
quest.description: You and Venti keep pushing on for the sake of some good wine. Cold corners, perilous places, strange sites... who knows what incidents await the two of you? Even more interestingly, you begin to realize that there is no common understanding of what a "Windblume" is.
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x60, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! Timaeus' alchemy store.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Oh, did you say my name?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Looks like I beat you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... did you do your homework, Timaeus? Hehehe... Paimon wants to hear it!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Uh... So sorry, I haven't gotten around to it yet...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Timaeus! Might I ask how you're progressing?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Huh? Traveler and friends! Oh, nice to see you again!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Sucrose has me deciphering an alchemical recipe, but my brain is doing backflips. I... I just don't understand it!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: So, in other words... no progress?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: *sigh* No.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ohh... Now that you mention it, I can't figure it out either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Is alchemy really that mysterious?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But of course! Alchemy is an ancient and mystical discipline. Yet with the passage of time, those that can be said to have mastered its secrets grow fewer and further between.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why not just ask the amazing Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Yes! That was my thinking too, but I believe that Mr. Albedo is still painting on the mountain, and we've got lots of research to do... *sigh* There's no getting around it.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: If you want my opinion, if Mr. Albedo can't figure out this recipe, nobody in Teyvat can. *sigh* Sucrose, what exactly is this recipe, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's a Windblume recipe I transcribed from an ancient book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! What if the Windblume isn't a naturally occurring plant after all, but an alchemical creation!?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh! Now that's an interesting take on the Windblume conundrum.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: You misunderstand, the book doesn't say anything about it being a recipe for a Windblume! The book... *sigh* Well, actually... it doesn't exactly have the appearance of a book anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: It's badly damaged and lots of information is missing. Only a few pages of scattered notes from the original volume have survived. That and a recipe written in some unknown language.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The author mentioned in the notes that the recipe was extremely precious. Timaeus and I are completely unable to decipher the content.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I know it might seem inconceivable, b—but... something about it being "extremely precious" made me think of Windblumes.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Huh? But...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, that's an active imagination.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Traveler, if I may be so bold...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Could you take this recipe to Mr. Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Mr. Albedo should be at the camp at the foot of the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahh, the mountain. Now there's a romantic location!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Windblume, the flower that alchemy made... Sounds exciting, Paimon needs to know the truth!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's get going, Albedo, here we come!

talks.objective: Go to the campsite at the foot of Dragonspine

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh? Traveler and Paimon? And who might this be?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is our Tone-Deaf Bard!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Venti will do just fine, but yes, I am a bard.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Greetings, I'm Albedo the alchemist.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is in full swing, people celebrating everywhere, and here you are all by yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Must be lonely...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, with the Windblume Festival in full swing, as you say, why would you be out here looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're helping Sucrose!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sucrose gave us some paper, she says there's a Windblume recipe from an ancient text on it! Neither she nor Timaeus can understand it, so we came looking for you!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A Windblume recipe?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see. This is an ancient language, it's no wonder Sucrose and Timaeus couldn't decipher it.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Even so, I don't believe this is a recipe for a Windblume.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So what could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I could only guess, I'm afraid. In order to reach a conclusion, we'll need to see the real thing.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sadly, my hands are full right now. But I can give you a list of ingredients, if you'd like to go gathering?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The recipe itself is from a forgotten era, but the thinking behind it is very innovative. Worth a try.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Okay! Job done.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Great work. Let's have a look, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm, seems we have everything we need. Now for the alchemical process. This shouldn't take long.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: There we have it.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... Is this the Windblume that Sucrose was talking about? It...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just a Sweet Flower!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Have a closer look. Are you sure it's the same as other Sweet Flowers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... now that you mention it, why is this Sweet Flower so big...?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: So this is the "Windblume" created by following this ancient recipe.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Haha, it really does make me think of Sucrose.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Huh, it does seem like something she would like.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Do Sweet Flowers this size even count as Sweet Flowers anymore?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I can say with certainty that yes, yes they do. Their essence is the same.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Sucrose said that she transcribed the recipe from an ancient book! Could it be that... there were Sweet Flowers around even in ancient times?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: There were indeed Sweet Flowers in antiquity. This species has a long history.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously!? Have Sweet Flowers... r—really existed all that time!?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Definitely something that Sucrose would like.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Well then, I must head further into the mountain — I still have painting to do. Perhaps you could pass this on?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Traveler, enjoy the celebrations.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh, Sucrose! We've got something for you.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Oh! You're back!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Timaeus, how's that homework coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Did you get the Windblume? Let me see, let me see!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Here's the flower he created, but Albedo said it's just—

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Wah! It's just like the Windblume in my dreams!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...It's just a Sweet Flower!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: No, no, hear me out! This is a perfect specimen from an ancient recipe. I saw it in my dreams...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The Tetratanic Sweet Flower!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... th—the what now?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: The seeds of the Tetratanic Sweet Flower are four times bigger than those of ordinary Sweet Flowers, and the Sweet Flowers that grow from them are, well, Tetratanic Sweet Flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Bigger, stronger, sweeter, and more beautiful — a perfect Teyvat species! Oh — and not to mention that the recipe comes from remote antiquity...

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: A perfect, magnificent flower from the far-flung past. Whatever people say, this is my Windblume!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Sucrose is... consistently Sucrose.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I must go and source some nutrients for my Windblume. Bye for now!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, who knew alchemy could generate such enthusiasm?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Now, Timaeus... Your homework?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Just finished, Sir. Here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooooh, here we go — Paimon's favorite part!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Timaeus, may I recite it?

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Ah!? You're gonna read it out loud? Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Haha, don't be embarrassed. *clears throat*... Here we go~

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "Hand in hand with you before the furnace\nThe flames fail to rise\nFor they are burning in my heart."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... Sounds so romantic... and you even tailored it to your profession! Great job!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Truly, a masterpiece beyond all expectation, Timaeus. You're a natural!

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Really...? Wow! I had no idea that someone like me could write love poems of any merit. It must have been Professor Venti's excellent guidance.

dialogues.speaker: Timaeus
dialogues.text: Professor, as soon as I'm done here, I'll sort out my tuition fee!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ahh, music to my ears, hehe!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Now... that's job satisfaction. And I guess that's everyone's homework collected... no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aren't we... missing someone?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Who could that be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmmmm... Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where did Bennett run off to?

talks.objective: Go to the Cathedral and talk to Barbara

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Barbara, we need to ask you something!

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon, Mr. Bard!

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Something terrible's happened. Bennett's gone missing!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Missing? You mean, he hasn't returned after leaving that day?

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Yes... What if he's in danger? We have no idea where he is...

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: ...The Thousand Winds Temple.

dialogues.speaker: Barbara
dialogues.text: Huh? Rosaria!

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: With you all in the Cathedral shouting at the top of your lungs, I could hear everything you were saying.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon remembers now, he said something like... "I've got it! The Thousand Winds Temple!"

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: There's no time to lose, let's head to the temple and investigate.

talks.objective: Go to the Thousand Winds Temple

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! We're here! Bennett, we've come to the rescue... Whoa, this cell has two sections!

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: See what I mean? Even they're surprised by this crazy cell!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Lucky you two got locked on opposite sides...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Huh, what a superior design... and presumably an ancient mechanism is involved somehow?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: There's gotta be a mechanism around here someplace. Quick! Go look for it!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: Stomach... rumbling...

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: ...You just ate the apple from my bag!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You two seem to have adjusted well to life in prison, we can leave you here if you like?

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: No no no no no, not funny! I'm begging you, alright? Please, find the mechanism!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Aaaand open sesame!

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Ah... Freedom at last!

choices.text: How did you get into this mess?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Very... unexpected...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Hahaha, I wouldn't call it unexpected. This was just a normal day for me.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Sorry.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ah... no need to apologize, it wasn't even your fault.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So, let's hear the story~

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Wait, what happened with that letter?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! It was just a false alarm, turns out some fans just wanted to get her attention so they could get a gift to her.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: What the...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: That's terrible, what kind of a person does that!? I've been locked up here a whole day thanks to them!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: S—Sorry...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Don't be, Razor! I—I didn't mean... Like I said, there's nothing to apologize for!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: It was my fault for being so hasty in the first place. I rushed off without giving the map a proper look and ended up in the complete wrong location... *sigh* After I left the Cathedral, I came straight to the area around the Thousand Winds Temple.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: But there were monsters everywhere, not to mention Ruin Guards! You know — those huge things, I guess you've seen them before.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: But as a first-rate adventurer, I was able to rely on my wits to evade them. Then I got to the temple itself...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: The moment I arrived here, I heard a monster's roar!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon's guessed the ending already...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I remember thinking it must be some villainous trap that the perpetrator had set for us. But was Bennett the adventurer, leader of Benny's Adventure Team about to back down? No way!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: So I charged straight in! ...That's when I found him inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Razor, what were you doing at the Thousand Winds Temple?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Wolvendom... many hunters.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Too noisy, so... I leave...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So you came all the way to the Thousand Winds Temple, then what? You were trapped by the mechanism?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: *grunts*

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Turns out it was no ordinary cell, what with the inner and outer sections. Of course, when I saw that Razor had been trapped inside, I had to rescue him... Then, all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: ...There was a huge crash as the other cell door came down.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, just as Paimon expected.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Anyway... why did you come to the Thousand Winds Temple?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Bennett, did you forget about your homework? I'm ready to collect my tuition fee, once I've corrected it of course.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Oh! The love poem! Of course I didn't forget!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: It's not like I had much else to do, being stuck in this cell all day and all night, so at some point I just started working on it. It's all finished now, even Razor reviewed it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh yeah? Razor, how did he do?

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Don't understand words. But feel... warm, tingly...

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Like... Wolfhook thorn...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Bennett, may I recite your work?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Oh... Sure! A taste of Bennett's wordsmanship, hehe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay! A round of applause for Bennett!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text:
"You and the Mare Jivari
So close and yet so far
One at the edge of the world
The other in the center of my heart
Wolfhook and dandelion
My Windblume offering to you."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Wolfhook?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Y—Yeah... Not bad... right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... it's definitely your style...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A marvelous work. Unpretentious and honest, sincere and evocative.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Thank you, thank you very much, Sir!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Bennett did good poem!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Haha, thanks to you too, Razor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Congratulations! Nice job!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, Wolfhook and dandelion...? Can they both be Windblumes?

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Oh, that was Razor's addition. I asked him: "What do you think the Windblume is?" Wolfhook was his answer.

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes! Wolfhook... good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, even berries count now?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A novel take indeed.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Ah... I'm so happy, today was lucky.

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Getting rescued against the odds, receiving praise for my poem... brilliant! Sir, as soon as we're back in Mondstadt, I'll buy you some wine!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Bennett's pretty easy to please...

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Hahaha, that's not quite it. I'm always so unlucky... so I'll take what I can get!

response.speaker: Razor
response.text: Yes! But... In future, be careful!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: Hey! You should talk! Hahaha...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Everyone, I have an announcement to make.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: All the poems from the fast-track class have now been collected!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: So to celebrate, let's go to the tavern and have a drink!

response.speaker: Bennett
response.text: I'm afraid Razor and I have to be going. He said he knows of some relatively unknown areas worth exploring and wants to show them to me. Have a great time, though!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Charles! It's us!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Welcome, have a seat wherever you like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh? Master Diluc?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Oh! I was about to finish this drink and go looking for you, but you've done the hard part for me.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Sure is lively in here!

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: It is the Windblume Festival after all. No one in Mondstadt who has the time and Mora is going to miss out on a trip to the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Traveler, will you have a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha, no pressure, it's not a requirement. Soaking up the festival atmosphere is the most important thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Master Jean wanted me to pass along this message... You've been chosen as this year's Windblume Star! Quite the honor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Windblume Star?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The Windblume Star is one of Mondstadt's greatest honors, normally only bestowed upon those who have made enormous sacrifices for Mondstadt... or who have truly proven themselves over the Windblume Festival period.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Since arriving in Mondstadt, you have offered invaluable support to its people. This is their way of saying thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I know you will receive it gracefully. Oh yes — and another thing.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: The Windblume Star must attend the Windblume Ceremony together with the Acting Grand Master. During the ceremony, you will represent the people of Mondstadt in making a Windblume offering to the Anemo Archon, Barbatos.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, which Windblume are you talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hah, a good question. Diluc, care to explain?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Passing on messages and deliberating over ceremonial details... Sounds more like your line of work, Kaeya.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: *sigh* No sense of humor.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Traveler, the Windblume is always chosen by the Windblume Star. So the flower offered to the Anemo Archon for this year's celebrations... is entirely up to you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... no pressure, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hey, where's the bartender? How come Master Diluc's mixing the drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: If it's Charles you're after, he's out on delivery.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Hahahaha, and who is most directly responsible for creating the demand for an alcohol-delivery service at this time of year in the first place?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: ...Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I see... So, what do you make of Master Diluc's mixing ability?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Why don't we ask the formidable Sister Rosaria... What do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: ...He's not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Formidable...? Did you guys have a fight?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I'd call it... a misunderstanding. I caught sight of a suspicious figure hurtling by the Knights of Favonius Headquarters. Fortunately, I discovered in good time that it was Miss Rosaria, and stayed my hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha! So the suspicious figure that day was Rosaria all along!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Folks in Mondstadt are on edge with you constantly on the prowl. You're no ordinary sister, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: Allow me to return the compliment, good Master Diluc. You're hardly a run-of-the-mill businessman yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Haha... My, such a formidable wit, too. But really, is there any here among us today who can't be said to possess a talent or two?

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Even the celebrated Honorary Knight has graced us with their presence tonight. Truly, a good day for a drink.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Well said! So Kaeya, about that tuition fee...

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: Please collect the goods from Diluc. Three bottles, as promised. They didn't come cheap.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The better the wine, the higher the price... just economics.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: How are you enjoying the Windblume Festival, Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's a fun time.

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: That's good to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: A toast, everyone. To a happy Windblume Festival and the free people of Mondstadt. Cheers!

dialogues.speaker: Crowd
dialogues.text: Cheers!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Hahaha, what a festival. Now, this won't drink itself!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Tone-Deaf Bard, spare a thought for other people! Paimon's looking for good food, not just good drink!

dialogues.speaker: Rosaria
dialogues.text: ...Taverns are so much more fun than Cathedrals. Speaking of which, doesn't everyone get time off for festivals like this? Why doesn't the Church give us time off?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I doubt Charles is nimble enough to handle both.

dialogues.speaker: Kaeya
dialogues.text: I was going to say, isn't it about time the tavern menu had a few starters and mains? What's a drink without something on the side?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Hmph... easier said than done.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: Ugh, I can't believe someone would come up with such a sinister mechanism!

dialogues.speaker: Razor
dialogues.text: *sigh* Hungry.

dialogues.speaker: Bennett
dialogues.text: I still have an apple in my bag. Here, you can have it.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Hehe! I've got high hopes!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ancient alchemical methods are very complicated... I hope Mr. Albedo is able to decipher it.
